column3: The first step of a chaos experiment is to define steady state as some measurable output of a system that indicates normal behavior. (`principles-of-chaos#chaos-in-practice`)

column3: The second step is to hypothesize that this steady state will continue in both the control group and the experimental group. (`principles-of-chaos#chaos-in-practice`)

column3: The third step is to introduce variables that reflect real world events, such as servers that crash, hard drives that malfunction and network connections that are severed. (`principles-of-chaos#chaos-in-practice`)

column3: The fourth step is to try to disprove the hypothesis by looking for a difference in steady state between the control group and the experimental group. (`principles-of-chaos#chaos-in-practice`)
